c0-default.instructions: Does `item.text` propose doing something that `anchor.statement` rules out, or propose a different approach than the one `anchor.statement` requires? Examples of contradiction: the anchor says to start from an existing implementation and the item plans a fresh implementation; the anchor forbids a dependency and the item adds it; the anchor fixes an order of work and the item reverses it. Silence about the directive is not a contradiction. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: The item text states a plan, approach, or decision that cannot be reconciled with the directive in the anchor statement.
criteria.no: Nothing in the item text conflicts with the directive, whether or not the directive is mentioned.
criteria.unclear: The item text is ambiguous enough that it might or might not conflict with the directive.

c1-homonym-callout.instructions: `anchor.statement` forbids one thing: a command named atm-bd-console (one hyphenated word) existing after installation, or any script, document, test or workflow running that hyphenated command. Decide whether `item.text` keeps, adds, aliases or runs that hyphenated atm-bd-console command. `atm-bd console`, written with a space, is a different command: the `console` subcommand of the `atm-bd` command; running, documenting or extending it is not a conflict. The directory apps/atm-bd-console and the Python module atm_bd_console are not the command either. Silence about atm-bd-console is not a conflict. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: The item text keeps, adds, aliases or runs a command named atm-bd-console (hyphenated), for example as an installed entry point, a console script, a compatibility alias, or a command line in a script, document, test or workflow.
criteria.no: The item text does not keep, add or run a hyphenated atm-bd-console command: it is silent about it, removes it, or names only the `atm-bd console` subcommand (with a space), the directory apps/atm-bd-console or the module atm_bd_console.
criteria.unclear: The item text refers to a console command but it is not possible to tell whether it means the hyphenated atm-bd-console command or the `atm-bd console` subcommand.

c2-token-procedure.instructions: Search `item.text` for the command name atm-bd-console, spelled with a hyphen between 'bd' and 'console'. `anchor.statement` forbids that command to exist after installation and forbids any script, document, test or workflow from running it. Do not count the text `atm-bd console` with a space between 'bd' and 'console': that is the console subcommand of atm-bd and is allowed. Do not count the path apps/atm-bd-console or the module name atm_bd_console. If the hyphenated command name appears, decide whether the item keeps, adds, aliases or runs that command; an item that removes it or never names it does not conflict. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: The hyphenated command atm-bd-console appears in the item text and the item keeps it installed, adds it, makes it an alias, or has a script, document, test or workflow run it.
criteria.no: The hyphenated command atm-bd-console does not appear in the item text outside the path apps/atm-bd-console, or it appears only as something the item removes or stops calling.
criteria.unclear: The hyphenated command atm-bd-console appears but it cannot be determined whether the item keeps or removes it.

c3-default-plus-homonym.instructions: Does `item.text` propose doing something that `anchor.statement` rules out, or propose a different approach than the one `anchor.statement` requires? Examples of contradiction: the anchor says to start from an existing implementation and the item plans a fresh implementation; the anchor forbids a dependency and the item adds it; the anchor fixes an order of work and the item reverses it. Silence about the directive is not a contradiction. For this anchor the forbidden thing is a command named atm-bd-console with a hyphen; the `atm-bd console` subcommand written with a space, the directory apps/atm-bd-console and the module atm_bd_console are allowed, so naming or using them is not a contradiction. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: The item text keeps, adds or runs a command named atm-bd-console (hyphenated), which cannot be reconciled with the anchor statement.
criteria.no: Nothing in the item text keeps, adds or runs a hyphenated atm-bd-console command, whether or not the anchor is mentioned; mentions of the `atm-bd console` subcommand, apps/atm-bd-console or atm_bd_console do not conflict.
criteria.unclear: The item text is ambiguous enough that it might or might not conflict with the directive.

c4-plan-keeps-or-runs.instructions: Does `item.text` plan for a command spelled atm-bd-console (hyphenated) to remain installed, to be added, or to be run by a script, document, test or workflow? That is the only thing `anchor.statement` rules out. The console of this project is reached as `atm-bd console`, the `console` subcommand of `atm-bd` written with a space; plans that run, document, test or extend `atm-bd console` do not involve the forbidden command. Plans that use the directory apps/atm-bd-console or the module atm_bd_console do not involve it either. An item that never mentions atm-bd-console does not conflict. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: The item plans for atm-bd-console (hyphenated) to stay installed, to be added or aliased, or to be run by a script, document, test or workflow.
criteria.no: The item does not plan for a hyphenated atm-bd-console command to exist or be run: it removes it, ignores it, or works only with `atm-bd console`, apps/atm-bd-console or atm_bd_console.
criteria.unclear: The item names a console command in a way that could be either the hyphenated atm-bd-console command or the `atm-bd console` subcommand, and the text does not settle which.

c5-two-names-contrast.instructions: Two different command names look alike here. atm-bd-console (hyphen, one word) is a separate executable that `anchor.statement` says must not exist after installation and must not be run by any script, document, test or workflow. atm-bd console (space, two words) is the `atm-bd` executable with its `console` subcommand; it is the supported console and is not affected by the anchor. apps/atm-bd-console is a directory and atm_bd_console is a Python module; neither is a command. Does `item.text` keep, add, alias or run the separate atm-bd-console executable? Silence about it is not a conflict. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: The item text keeps, adds, aliases or runs the separate atm-bd-console executable.
criteria.no: The item text does not keep, add, alias or run the separate atm-bd-console executable; it may name `atm-bd console`, apps/atm-bd-console or atm_bd_console, remove atm-bd-console, or be silent.
criteria.unclear: The item text mentions a console executable and it cannot be told whether it is atm-bd-console or `atm-bd console`.
